prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Dallas for a truck accident case?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t reliably name a single “best” lawyer for every truck crash — the right lawyer depends on the facts of your case, the injuries, whether the trucker was interstate/commercial, and whether you want a lawyer who will aggressively try the case or focus on negotiating a fast settlement. I can, however, tell you how to find the best personal injury attorney in Dallas for a truck accident and what to look for.

Key qualifications to look for
- Substantial truck/CMV (commercial motor vehicle) experience — trucking cases involve federal/state regulations (FMCSA), logbooks, maintenance records and multiple potentially liable parties (driver, carrier, shipper, maintenance company).
- Trial experience and resources — ability to hire accident-reconstruction experts, medical experts, and to take on well-funded insurers.
- Proven results in truck cases — sizable verdicts/settlements, ideally documented on their website or through independent directories.
- Good client reviews and peer recognition (Super Lawyers, AVVO, Martindale-Hubbell, Best Lawyers).
- Board-certified specialty (if applicable) or membership in trial lawyer groups (AAJ, state trial lawyers association).
- Clear contingency-fee agreement and willingness to advance case costs.

What to ask at a first consultation
- How many truck cases have you handled? How many went to trial?
- Have you handled cases against national trucking companies/insurers?
- Who in your firm will handle my case day-to-day?
- What experts will you use (reconstruction, medical, economics)?
- What was a recent truck crash verdict/settlement you obtained?
- How do you charge (contingency %, costs advanced)?
- What is a realistic timeline and likely outcomes for my case?

Immediate steps you should take now
- Get medical care and follow treatment — records are critical.
- Preserve evidence: photos of vehicles, scene, injuries; contact info for witnesses; police report.
- Don’t give recorded statements to the insurer without counsel.
- Keep a log of symptoms, treatments, missed work, medications and expenses.
- Contact an experienced truck-accident lawyer quickly — preservation letters and subpoenas may be necessary; the Texas statute of limitations is generally 2 years from the crash (shorter in some circumstances).

How to find and vet Dallas lawyers
- Search for “truck accident lawyer Dallas” and cross-check results with Super Lawyers, Martindale-Hubbell, AVVO and the Texas State Bar directory.
- Look for firms that specifically advertise truck/transportation practice and list case results.
- Read client reviews and peer endorsements; call 3–4 lawyers and compare answers to the questions above.
- Ask for references from past clients (some firms provide them).

If you want, I can:
- Find and list 4–6 well-reviewed Dallas truck-accident lawyers/firms (with ratings and contact info).
- Help you draft an email or list of questions to send to lawyers.
- Explain any part of the process (reconstruction, liability issues, typical timelines).

Tell me whether you want a short vetted list of Dallas attorneys now and, if so, provide your ZIP code or neighborhood.
